summary:
Fire Drill is a web app that ranks 19 NASA PSI microgravity combustion investigations by how closely their tested conditions match a chosen crewed environment (oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity). It uses real NASA data, including 1,139 test runs.

For "Flame in Freefall," it shows which past experiments are most relevant and where PSI records do not include data. Every value shows its source, unknown values stay "not recorded," and scores show their math.

This matters because spacecraft fire safety depends on knowing what has actually been tested. Fire Drill makes the gaps visible so researchers can see where evidence is thin before planning the next experiment. It is a research-navigation aid, not a fire predictor or NASA guidance.
details:
What it does and how it works
FlameMap is an SI-powered briefing on NASA's microgravity fire experiments for crewed missions. You pick where the crew will live: station cabin, lunar habitat, rover, Mars habitat, spacesuit, NASA's Exploration Atmosphere, or your own oxygen, pressure and gravity values. You also pick the task: preventing, detecting or putting out a fire. An AI briefing then explains three things: what the closest of 19 flight investigations in NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database found, what has never been tested in that environment, and what to read next. Every sentence links to its NASA source. Visitors can also ask questions in their own words on "Ask the evidence", a conversation over 66 checked answers.

Behind the briefing is a transparent ranking. We read the PSI records and their experimental tables (1,993 rows), converted units, and stored each condition with its source and a confidence label. Each study's score is plain arithmetic, the distance between the chosen environment and the tested range for each factor, and the app shows that math for every score. If a study didn't record a condition, it counts as untested, so missing data never raises a score. Other pages include an evidence map of 875 test runs by oxygen and pressure, key findings quoted from NASA sources, side-by-side comparison, and CSV/JSON export for modeling.

How the AI is used, and kept honest
Claude (Opus 5.5, through Claude Code) wrote the briefings, answers, findings and related-study reasons when the site was built, using only the PSI records, NASA's Researcher's Guide and the computed data. A script then checks every sentence. The build fails if any quote isn't word-for-word in its source, any number isn't in the data the sentence cites, or any study is named without a citation. The current text passes with 295 sentences, 667 citations and 311 numbers checked. A team member reviewed the text and signed off on a hash of it, so any later change fails the build until someone reviews it again. AI never sets a ranking score.

We chose this design so the site needs no API key, no server and no cost per visit, and nothing reaches a reader before it has been checked. Questions are matched to the checked answers by meaning, using a small open embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) that runs entirely in the browser. That model compares questions; it doesn't write text. The answer layer is built so a live mode can be added later, either with a visitor's own key or through a hosted proxy, with the same checks running in the browser.

Benefits and intended impact
Moon and Mars habitats are planned with at least 30% oxygen at reduced pressure, which is far more flammable than station air. FlameMap shows how little evidence covers those conditions. For a lunar habitat:

  • No solid-fuel test in PSI goes above 22.2% oxygen.
  • None of the 19 investigations ran at partial gravity.

Researchers, engineers and students get a cited starting point in seconds instead of searching scattered records, and they see where new experiments are most needed. It is a research-navigation aid, not a safety certification.

Tools, languages and software
TypeScript, React, Vite, Recharts, Node.js, Vitest (22 unit tests), and Transformers.js with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for in-browser search. Claude Code was used for planning, code and the AI-written text. The site is a static site on GitHub Pages, deployed by GitHub Actions. No special hardware was used.

How it is creative
Most AI dashboards call a model live and hope the answer is right. FlameMap does the reverse: the AI writes ahead of time, a machine checks every claim, and a person signs off. The result is AI-written text you can audit, with no keys and no runtime cost. FlameMap also treats missing evidence as a finding and puts "what has never been tested here" next to the results.

Factors we considered

  • Trust: every sentence is cited and checked, and all AI text is labeled.
  • Transparency: arithmetic ranks, AI explains.
  • Honest handling of missing data: untested conditions are never assumed safe.
  • Cost and access: no keys, no server, works on a phone.
  • Privacy: questions never leave the browser.
  • Extensibility: a live-answer mode can be added later.
  • Clear limits: it does not predict fire behavior.
